title: Algebraic upper shriek: polynomial models, coinduction, composition and flat base change
statement: For a finite type map $\varphi:R\to A$ of commutative Noetherian rings, choose a polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$. There is a functor $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$, well defined up to isomorphism, whose chosen presentation model is $R\operatorname{Hom}_{P}(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$ for $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Here $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,-)$ denotes derived coinduction with its natural $A$-module structure. The following comparisons hold. (i) For a surjection $\varphi$, $\varphi^!=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,-)$, right adjoint to restriction of scalars; forgetting the $A$-action gives the ordinary derived Hom over $R$. For any ring maps $R\to B\to C$, derived coinduction composes canonically, compatibly with its evaluation counits. (ii) For finite type Noetherian maps $R\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{b}C$, there is an isomorphism $b^!a^!K\cong(ba)^!K$ for $K\in D^+(R)$; the identity map can be modeled by the identity functor. (iii) For a flat map $R\to R'$ of Noetherian rings, $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ and $\varphi':R'\to A'$, there is an isomorphism $\varphi^!K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\cong(\varphi')^!(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')$ for $K\in D^+(R)$. (iv) If $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an open immersion, then $\varphi^!K\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$. These assertions concern chosen polynomial models and isomorphisms, and do not assert a canonical orientation for different polynomial presentations.

proof.text: Write $C_B^T$ for derived coinduction. The cited adjunction gives its functor, underlying Hom and evaluation counit. For $R\to B\to C$, the two adjunction bijections give $\operatorname{Hom}_C(N,C_C^BC_B^R K)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,K)$ naturally; hence they identify $C_C^BC_B^R$ with $C_C^R$. On Hom models the comparison and inverse are $h\mapsto(c\mapsto[b\mapsto h(bc)])$ and $v\mapsto(c\mapsto v(c)(1))$; the counit is $v(1)(1)$.

source.place: Tags 0A70, 0A71 and 0C0F, restriction--coinduction adjunctions and their composition.

proof.text: Define $F_P(K)=C_A^P(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$. The refinement lemma identifies this with the model after adjoining variables whose images lift to $P$. Two surjective presentations have a common polynomial presentation, so give isomorphic functors. For a surjection take $P=R$; for the identity evaluation $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,I)=I$ gives the identity model.

source.place: Tags 0BZI and 0BZJ, polynomial models and common refinements.

proof.text: For (iii), set $P'=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $A'=A\otimes_RR'$. The finite-type Noetherian theorem makes $P$ Noetherian. Polynomial rings are free over their base by monomials; $P\to P'$ is flat since tensoring is tensoring over $R$ with $R'$. Thus $M=K\otimes_RP$ is bounded below. Apply the quotient base-change lemma and shift by $n$; both coefficient complexes are $K\otimes_RP'$.

For (ii), choose $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$, $Q=P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, $Q'=B[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\twoheadrightarrow C$. The same quotient comparison for $P\to Q$, applied to $M=K\otimes_RP$, gives $C_B^P(M)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}Q'\cong C_{Q'}^Q(K\otimes_RQ)$. Apply $C_C^{Q'}$, use step 1 and add shifts $n+m$: the result is the model for $R\to C$.

source.place: Tag 0BZT (lemma-composition-shriek-algebraic); Q′ in its first displayed equality.

proof.text: For (iv), an open immersion has isomorphic local rings, so the affine criterion makes $R\to A$ flat. It is a monomorphism by restriction of its structure sheaf, hence its self fibre product is itself. The affine fibre-product formula gives $A\otimes_RA=A$. The flat polynomial-quotient theorem makes $A$ perfect over $P$; the graph-dual lemma gives $\omega=C_A^P(P)[n]\cong A$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0C0H (lemma-upper-shriek-localize), flat self-base-change and polynomial dualizing object.

proof.text: Perfect coinduction--tensor comparison gives $F_P(K)\cong(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}\omega\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$. Rebracket on a K-flat $R$-representative $F$: $(F\otimes_RP)\otimes_P\omega=F\otimes_R\omega$, preserving the $A$-action. This works for unbounded $K$; $A=0$ and zero variables give the zero and identity cases. The complex $F\otimes_RP$ is K-flat over $P$: tensoring an acyclic $P$-complex $N$ gives $F\otimes_RN$, which is acyclic.
